messages.author: 4930c9beda1eda3c
messages.subject: comparing r/qtl to multiQTL
parts:
I've been mapping with MultiQTL but switched to r/qtl recently because
I have one binary trait (which MultiQTL can't deal with). I think
I've been running r/qtl correctly but I can't recreate the results I
got for the other, normally distributed traits analyzed with the
MultiQTL software. Has anyone else tried to compare these two
programs? I know they run different algorithms but I expected to get
somewhat similar results for the normally distributed traits. Another
little wrinkle...I have an outcrossed mapping family but I am
analyzing the sexes separately so have been using the backcross model
in both MultiQTL and r/qtl. Not sure if that would affect the
comparisons between programs though.

thanks

Erin

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] comparing r/qtl to multiQTL
parts:
You don't give us too much to go on. Just how different are the
results?
It's hard to say, without looking at the results and the data, why the
programs are giving you different answers.

I'm not sure how you would analyze the outcross data as two separate
backcrosses; I've seen that done for genetic map construction, but for
QTL mapping it seems (to me) a bit odd.

regards,
karl
